text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Treaty to trim Ottawa's power: Equal-treatment rules for foreign firms could limit research, job-creation targets.
- Megacity meets blizzard of paper: Thousands of amendments introduced in effort to stall proposed Ontario legislation.
- Canada reviews position on China: Backing for rights criticism in question.
- Commander pleads guilty to Somalia-related charge: Caie makes deal for his part in document-tampering scheme.
- Back-room deals spice Iranian elections: With President Rafsanjani stepping down, an outsider with liberal tendencies has jolted the conservative front-runner from complacency.
- TCPL plans C$1-billion pipeline: To team up with American utility to supply gas to U.S. Midwest despite rival proposal.
- Bre-X trading overloads TSE, again: Exchange considers unique short-term solution to problem.
- St. Laurent strikes deal for 5 U.S. mills: US$500-million purchase from Chesapeake would double its size, boost its packaging market share.
- C$7.5 million parachutes land on Southam.
- Microsoft's Expedia hits Canada: On-line travel service not expected to hurt traditional agents.
- TCPL plans US$1-billion push: New 1,300-kilometre natural gas pipeline challenges Alliance link to Midwest.
- Bre-X throws spanner in TSE works.
